units.title: Tools of Geometry
units.blurb: Undefined terms and definitions, distance and midpoints, and compass-and-straightedge constructions.

units.title: Reasoning and Proof
units.blurb: Use if-then logic and the properties of equality to write proofs about lines and angles.

units.title: Rigid Motions
units.blurb: Define transformations precisely, compose them, and find symmetries.

units.title: Triangle Congruence
units.blurb: Prove triangles congruent and use congruent parts.

units.title: Properties of Triangles
units.blurb: Prove triangle theorems and find the special points of a triangle.

units.title: Quadrilaterals and Polygons
units.blurb: Find polygon angle sums and prove properties of parallelograms and special quadrilaterals.

units.title: Similarity
units.blurb: Use dilations to define similarity, prove triangles similar, and use proportional segments.

units.title: Right Triangles and Trigonometry
units.blurb: Use special right triangles and the trig ratios to solve triangles.

units.title: Circles
units.blurb: Learn arcs, angles, chords and tangents, arc length and sector area, and circle equations.

units.title: Area, Volume and Modeling
units.blurb: Explain the volume formulas, find surface areas, scale solids, and model real objects.

topics.title: Points, Lines and Planes
topics.short: Build every definition from point, line, plane and distance.
topics.trouble: Students treat a drawing as proof that lines meet or are equal, instead of using definitions.

topics.title: Distance and Midpoint Formulas
topics.short: Distance comes from the Pythagorean theorem; the midpoint averages the coordinates.
topics.trouble: Students subtract the coordinates to find a midpoint, or forget to square the negative differences.

topics.title: Angles and Angle Bisectors
topics.short: Name and measure angles, and split them in half.

topics.title: Copying and Bisecting with Compass and Straightedge
topics.short: Copy a segment and an angle, and bisect both.
topics.trouble: Students change the compass width partway through a construction.

topics.title: Constructing Perpendicular and Parallel Lines
topics.short: Construct a perpendicular bisector and a parallel through a point.

topics.title: Constructing Polygons in a Circle
topics.short: Inscribe an equilateral triangle, a square and a regular hexagon.

topics.title: If-Then Statements
topics.short: Write the converse, inverse and contrapositive, and find counterexamples.
topics.trouble: Students assume a statement's converse is true whenever the statement is.

topics.title: Properties of Equality as Reasons
topics.short: Justify each algebra step with a property.

topics.title: Writing a Proof
topics.short: Chain given facts, definitions and theorems to reach a conclusion.
topics.trouble: Students use what they are trying to prove as a reason, or trust how the diagram looks.

topics.title: Proving Theorems about Lines and Angles
topics.short: Prove vertical angles are equal and that parallel lines give equal angles, and their converses.
topics.trouble: Students use a parallel-line angle fact to prove lines are parallel, which reverses the logic.

topics.title: Transformations as Functions
topics.short: A transformation is a rule that sends each point to an image point.
topics.trouble: Students think a dilation keeps lengths, or that a stretch is a rigid motion.

topics.title: Precise Definitions of Rigid Motions
topics.short: Define rotations, reflections and translations with angles, circles, perpendiculars and parallels.

topics.title: Symmetries of Polygons
topics.short: Find the rotations and reflections that carry a polygon onto itself.
topics.trouble: Students count a 360° turn but miss rotations like 72° for a regular pentagon.

topics.title: Composing Transformations
topics.short: Apply a sequence of transformations and find one that maps a figure to another.
topics.trouble: Students assume the order of transformations never matters.

topics.title: Congruence and Rigid Motions
topics.short: Two figures are congruent when a rigid motion maps one onto the other.

topics.title: Corresponding Parts
topics.short: In △ABC ≅ △DEF, the letters tell which parts match.
topics.trouble: Students match parts by position on the page instead of by the order of the letters.

topics.title: SSS, SAS and ASA
topics.short: Three well-chosen parts are enough, and rigid motions show why.
topics.trouble: Students accept SSA or AAA as proof of congruence.

topics.title: AAS and Hypotenuse-Leg
topics.short: Two more shortcuts, including one for right triangles.

topics.title: Proofs with Congruent Triangles
topics.short: Prove triangles congruent, then use matching parts.
topics.trouble: Students use matching parts as a reason before proving the triangles congruent.

topics.title: Triangle Sum and Exterior Angle Proofs
topics.short: Prove the angle sum is 180° and the exterior angle theorem.

topics.title: Isosceles and Equilateral Triangles
topics.short: Base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal, and the converse holds.
topics.trouble: Students mark the wrong pair of angles as the base angles.

topics.title: Perpendicular Bisectors and the Circumcenter
topics.short: Points on a perpendicular bisector are equally far from the endpoints.

topics.title: Incenter, Centroid and Orthocenter
topics.short: Angle bisectors, medians and altitudes each meet at one point.
topics.trouble: Students mix up medians and altitudes, or think every center lies inside the triangle.

topics.title: Triangle Midsegments
topics.short: A midsegment is parallel to the third side and half as long.

topics.title: Polygon Angle Sums
topics.short: Split a polygon into triangles: (n − 2) × 180°.
topics.trouble: Students think the exterior angles add to more for polygons with more sides, when the sum is always 360°.

topics.title: Properties of Parallelograms
topics.short: Opposite sides and angles are equal, and diagonals bisect each other.
topics.trouble: Students assume the diagonals of every parallelogram are equal or perpendicular.

topics.title: Proving a Quadrilateral Is a Parallelogram
topics.short: Use one of the tests, like two pairs of opposite sides equal.

topics.title: Rectangles, Rhombuses and Squares
topics.short: Equal diagonals mean a rectangle; perpendicular diagonals mean a rhombus.
topics.trouble: Students think a quadrilateral with perpendicular diagonals must be a rhombus.

topics.title: Proofs with Coordinates
topics.short: Use slope, distance and midpoint to prove facts about figures.
topics.trouble: Students place figures at awkward coordinates and get lost in the algebra.

topics.title: Properties of Dilations
topics.short: A dilation keeps lines parallel and multiplies lengths by k.
topics.trouble: Students think a dilation also multiplies angles by k.

topics.title: Similarity Through Transformations
topics.short: Two figures are similar if a dilation and rigid motions map one to the other.

topics.title: Proving AA Similarity
topics.short: Two pairs of equal angles make triangles similar.

topics.title: SSS and SAS Similarity
topics.short: Proportional sides, with or without an included angle, prove similarity.
topics.trouble: Students compare sides in the wrong order and get ratios that do not match.

topics.title: The Triangle Proportionality Theorem
topics.short: A line parallel to one side divides the other two sides proportionally.
topics.trouble: Students set the small segment against the whole side on one side and against a part on the other.

topics.title: Dividing a Segment in a Ratio
topics.short: Find the point that splits a segment in the ratio a : b.
topics.trouble: Students go a/b of the way instead of a/(a + b) of the way.

topics.title: Similar Right Triangles and the Geometric Mean
topics.short: The altitude to the hypotenuse makes three similar triangles.

topics.title: Proving the Pythagorean Theorem with Similarity
topics.short: Use the three similar triangles to prove a² + b² = c².

topics.title: 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 Triangles
topics.short: Their sides are in fixed ratios: 1 : 1 : √2 and 1 : √3 : 2.
topics.trouble: Students put √3 on the hypotenuse or match it to the wrong leg.

topics.title: Sine, Cosine and Tangent
topics.short: Similar triangles make side ratios depend only on the angle.
topics.trouble: Students name opposite and adjacent from the wrong angle.

topics.title: Sine and Cosine of Complementary Angles
topics.short: sin A = cos(90° − A).

topics.title: Solving Right Triangles
topics.short: Find missing sides with trig ratios and the Pythagorean theorem.
topics.trouble: Students set up sin x = 8/x incorrectly, or leave the calculator in radian mode.

topics.title: Finding Angles with Inverse Trig
topics.short: Use sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹ and tan⁻¹ to find an angle from a ratio.
topics.trouble: Students read sin⁻¹ as 1/sin.

topics.title: Angles of Elevation and Depression
topics.short: Model heights and distances with right triangles.
topics.trouble: Students measure the angle of depression from the vertical instead of the horizontal.

topics.title: Triangle Area with Sine
topics.short: Area = ½ab sin C.

topics.title: The Law of Sines
topics.short: Sides are proportional to the sines of their opposite angles.
topics.trouble: Students pair a side with an angle that is not opposite it.

topics.title: The Law of Cosines
topics.short: c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C extends the Pythagorean theorem.
topics.trouble: Students combine a² + b² − 2ab before multiplying by cos C.

topics.title: Parts of a Circle
topics.short: Radius, diameter, chord, arc, tangent and secant.

topics.title: Central Angles and Arcs
topics.short: An arc's measure equals its central angle; all circles are similar.

topics.title: Inscribed Angles
topics.short: An inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc.
topics.trouble: Students set an inscribed angle equal to its arc, as if it were a central angle.

topics.title: Tangent Lines
topics.short: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

topics.title: Inscribed Quadrilaterals
topics.short: Opposite angles of an inscribed quadrilateral add to 180°.

topics.title: Arc Length
topics.short: An arc is a fraction of the circumference: (θ/360) · 2πr.
topics.trouble: Students use the diameter in the formula, or forget to take the fraction of the circle.

topics.title: Sector Area
topics.short: A sector is a fraction of the circle's area.
topics.trouble: Students confuse sector area with arc length.

topics.title: Equation of a Circle
topics.short: (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r² comes from the distance formula.
topics.trouble: Students read the center of (x + 2)² + (y − 1)² = 9 as (2, −1), or take 9 as the radius.

topics.title: Finding the Center by Completing the Square
topics.short: Rewrite x² + y² + Dx + Ey + F = 0 in center-radius form.
topics.trouble: Students add the completing numbers to one side only.

topics.title: Parabola from Focus and Directrix
topics.short: A parabola is all points equally far from a point and a line.

topics.title: Area of Regular Polygons
topics.short: Area = ½ × apothem × perimeter.

topics.title: Perimeter and Area on the Coordinate Plane
topics.short: Use the distance formula to find perimeters and areas.

topics.title: Cavalieri's Principle
topics.short: Solids with equal cross-sections at every height have equal volume.

topics.title: Volume of Pyramids, Cones and Spheres
topics.short: Use V = ⅓Bh for pyramids and cones and V = (4/3)πr³ for spheres.
topics.trouble: Students use the slant height in place of the height.

topics.title: Surface Area of Solids
topics.short: Find surface areas of prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres.
topics.trouble: Students use the height instead of the slant height for the lateral area of a cone or pyramid.

topics.title: Cross Sections and Solids of Revolution
topics.short: Identify slices of solids and the solid made by spinning a shape.

topics.title: Scaling Area and Volume
topics.short: Scale lengths by k: areas scale by k², volumes by k³.
topics.trouble: Students double the volume when every length is doubled, when it grows eight times.

topics.title: Modeling, Density and Design
topics.short: Model objects with shapes, use density, and solve design problems.
topics.trouble: Students mix units such as people per square mile and people per square kilometer.
